idle.baumannSectionDesc: Based on the Baumann Skin Type classification (Dr. Leslie Baumann), used by dermatologists worldwide, your skin is analyzed across 4 axes: Oily/Dry (O/D), Sensitive/Resistant (S/R), Pigmented/Non-pigmented (P/N), and Wrinkle-prone/Tight (W/T). Just like MBTI, 4 letters reveal your unique skin identity.
idle.howTitle: How does AI skin analysis work?
howSteps: Analyzes skin tone, pores, radiance & spots in your selfie using multi-spectrum analysis
AI quantifies 10 skin indicators on a 0–100 scale
Determines your personal skin type based on Baumann's 4-axis scores
Delivers personalized ingredient, routine & product recommendations for your Baumann type

polluted.title: High Pollution — Double Cleanse
polluted.body: Fine particles clog pores. Use an oil cleanser first, then a foam cleanser, and follow with an antioxidant serum.

polluted.title: Shield Up Before Heading Out
polluted.body: On polluted days, apply a mineral sunscreen as a physical barrier. Cleanse immediately when you get home.

snowy.title: Winter Skin Intensive Care
snowy.body: Snow reflects UV rays strongly. Strengthen your skin barrier with ceramide cream and don't skip sunscreen.

snowy.title: Watch Out for Snowmelt Water
snowy.body: Melted snow can irritate skin. After coming inside, cleanse with lukewarm water and apply a thick moisturizer.

rainy.title: Rainy Day Light Moisture
rainy.body: High humidity can increase sebum. Swap heavy creams for a light gel moisturizer to keep skin balanced.

rainy.title: Exfoliate on Wet Days
rainy.body: Humidity causes skin cells to swell. A gentle weekly exfoliation helps clear away buildup and keeps pores clear.

foggy.title: Foggy Day — Cleanse Well
foggy.body: Atmospheric particles can irritate pores. Do a thorough but gentle cleanse when you get home.

foggy.title: Barrier Protection in Fog
foggy.body: Fine particles settle on skin in foggy conditions. Use a non-comedogenic sunscreen as a shield before going out.

cold.title: Cold Wind — Protect Your Barrier
cold.body: Cold air strips moisture fast. Apply a ceramide-rich cream before heading out to shield your skin barrier.

cold.title: Indoor Heating Dries Skin Too
cold.body: Heating drops indoor humidity fast. Keep a facial mist on your desk and spritz throughout the day.

sunny_hot.title: Intense UV — Reapply Sunscreen!
sunny_hot.body: Reapply SPF 50+ every 2 hours. Add a vitamin C serum in the morning for extra antioxidant defense.

sunny_hot.title: Choose Cooling Suncare Today
sunny_hot.body: Opt for water-resistant SPF in the heat. Touch up with powder sunscreen and blotting paper for easy reapplication.

sunny.title: Don't Skip Sunscreen
sunny.body: Clear days mean UVA/UVB exposure. Layer vitamin C serum under sunscreen for dual protection.

sunny.title: Check Your UV Index
sunny.body: Any UV reading above 3 means sunscreen is non-negotiable — even through windows indoors.

dry.title: Low Humidity — Layer Moisture
dry.body: Air is dry! Layer essence → serum → cream to lock in hydration throughout the day.

dry.title: Boost Indoor Humidity
dry.body: Dry outdoor air affects indoors too. Run a humidifier and layer hyaluronic acid serum under your moisturizer.

humid.title: High Humidity — Go Light
humid.body: Skip heavy creams and opt for a gel moisturizer or hydrating mist to keep skin comfortable.

humid.title: Balance Oils with a BHA Toner
humid.body: High humidity triggers excess sebum. A BHA toner helps manage shine — finish with a non-comedogenic SPF.

cloudy.title: Cloudy Still Means UV
cloudy.body: Clouds let through up to 80% of UV rays. Sunscreen is still essential on overcast days.

cloudy.title: UVA Penetrates Through Clouds
cloudy.body: Overcast skies don't block UVA rays. An SPF-infused primer or BB cream gives quick lightweight protection.
